intro.tagline: An interactive 3D petri dish and microbiology lab simulator.
intro.placeholderNote: Early build: one dish, one organism, loop streaking and time controls. This page will become the full introduction and instructions.
intro.disclaimer: Agar is an educational model. It is not a substitute for real laboratory work.

tools.title: Tool
tools.handHelp: Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, right-drag to pan.
tools.loopHelp: Drag on the agar to streak. Right-drag to orbit.
tools.swabHelp: Drag on the agar to spread a lawn, or swab the whole plate at once.
tools.discHelp: Click the agar to press a disc onto it.
tools.inspectHelp: Click a colony to zoom in on it, then prepare a slide for the microscope.
tools.spreadHelp: Pipette a diluted culture onto the agar and spread it evenly.

tools.countHelp: Click colonies to tick them off, or count automatically.

microscope.title: Microscope
microscope.empty: Nothing but clean agar on this slide. Take the sample from a colony.
microscope.note: A visual model of cell shape, size, arrangement and division. Division is shown much faster than real time, and the 1000× view is enlarged so that single cells are easy to see.

inspect.pick: Click a colony to look at it closely.

escherichia-coli.fact: A gut bacterium and the workhorse of molecular biology. Ferments lactose, so it grows pink to red on MacConkey agar.

staphylococcus-aureus.fact: Golden colonies of cocci in grape-like clusters. Beta-hemolytic on blood agar and turns mannitol salt agar yellow.

staphylococcus-epidermidis.fact: A harmless resident of human skin. White colonies, no hemolysis, and no colour change on mannitol salt agar.

bacillus-subtilis.fact: A spore-forming soil bacterium. Its colonies are dry, dull and wrinkled with an irregular edge; a frequent airborne contaminant.

pseudomonas-aeruginosa.fact: Flat, spreading colonies with a metallic sheen. Releases a blue-green pigment that soaks into the agar, and smells of grapes.

serratia-marcescens.fact: Famous for its blood-red pigment, prodigiosin, which it makes at room temperature but not at body temperature.

micrococcus-luteus.fact: Slow-growing, bright yellow colonies of cocci in tetrads. Lives on skin and dust and often lands on open plates.

chromobacterium-violaceum.fact: A soil and water bacterium whose colonies are deep violet from the pigment violacein.

proteus-mirabilis.fact: So motile that it swarms across the agar in waves, leaving concentric rings instead of separate colonies.

streptococcus-pyogenes.fact: Tiny grey colonies of cocci in chains, each surrounded by a wide, completely clear zone of beta-hemolysis.

streptococcus-pneumoniae.fact: Lancet-shaped cocci in pairs. Small glistening colonies with a greenish zone of alpha-hemolysis.

klebsiella-pneumoniae.fact: A thick capsule makes its colonies large, domed and slimy. Ferments lactose: pink and mucoid on MacConkey agar.

salmonella-enterica.fact: A motile enteric rod that does not ferment lactose, so its colonies stay colourless on MacConkey agar.

candida-albicans.fact: A yeast, not a bacterium: large oval cells that bud. Cream, pasty colonies that prefer Sabouraud agar.

penicillium-chrysogenum.fact: The blue-green mold behind penicillin. Velvety colonies with a white growing edge that inhibit nearby bacteria.

aspergillus-niger.fact: A fast mold that starts white and turns black as its spore heads form.

rhizopus-stolonifer.fact: Black bread mold. Cottony growth that can fill a whole plate in two to three days.

nutrient-agar.name: Nutrient agar
nutrient-agar.about: General-purpose medium; most non-fastidious organisms grow.

lb-agar.name: LB agar
lb-agar.about: Rich general-purpose medium, the standard for E. coli work.

blood-agar.name: Blood agar
blood-agar.about: Enriched with sheep blood; shows alpha, beta or gamma hemolysis.

macconkey-agar.name: MacConkey agar
macconkey-agar.about: Selects Gram-negative enterics; lactose fermenters turn pink.

mueller-hinton-agar.name: Mueller-Hinton agar
mueller-hinton-agar.about: Standard medium for antibiotic disc testing.

sabouraud-agar.name: Sabouraud dextrose agar
sabouraud-agar.about: Acidic, sugar-rich; favours yeasts and molds.

mannitol-salt-agar.name: Mannitol salt agar
mannitol-salt-agar.about: High salt selects staphylococci; mannitol fermenters turn it yellow.

pure-culture.title: Pure Culture
pure-culture.goal: Unknown A is a mixture of two bacteria. Streak it out so that each one grows as separate, pure colonies.

criteria.streaked: Streak Unknown A onto a plate
criteria.isolated: Obtain isolated, pure colonies of both organisms

fleming.title: Fleming's Accident
fleming.goal: Reproduce the observation that led to penicillin: a mold that keeps Staphylococcus aureus from growing near it.

criteria.staph: Add Staphylococcus aureus to the same plate and let it grow
criteria.inhibited: Show that S. aureus grows far from the mold but not near it

kirby-bauer.title: Kirby-Bauer
kirby-bauer.goal: Find out which antibiotics work against Unknown B with a disc-diffusion test.

criteria.lawn: Swab a lawn of Unknown B on Mueller-Hinton agar
criteria.discs: Place discs of at least three different antibiotics
criteria.incubated: Incubate overnight until the lawn has grown
criteria.measured: Measure the zone of at least three antibiotics

temperature.title: Temperature Matters
temperature.goal: Serratia marcescens looks different at room temperature and at body temperature. Show it.

criteria.inoculated: Inoculate two plates with Serratia marcescens
criteria.cool: Grow one for a day at 30 °C or below
criteria.warm: Grow the other for a day at 36 °C or above

differential-media.title: Differential Media
differential-media.goal: Use MacConkey agar to tell a lactose fermenter from a non-fermenter.

criteria.fermenter: Grow a lactose fermenter on it (pink colonies)
criteria.nonFermenter: Grow a non-fermenter on it (colourless colonies)

blood-agar.title: Blood Agar Detective
blood-agar.goal: Find organisms that show each of the three kinds of hemolysis on blood agar.

criteria.beta: Beta: complete clearing around the colonies
criteria.gamma: Gamma: no change to the blood

count-cfu.title: Count the CFUs
count-cfu.goal: Work out how many live cells per millilitre are in the E. coli culture, using a dilution and a spread plate.

criteria.spread: Make a spread plate from a dilution
criteria.countable: Get a plate with 30 to 300 separate colonies
criteria.plausible: Arrive at a CFU/mL within threefold of the true value

aseptic.title: Aseptic Master
aseptic.goal: Inoculate a plate and incubate it for a day with nothing growing on it except what you put there.

criteria.flamed: Use only a freshly flamed loop

mystery.title: Mystery Microbe
mystery.goal: Identify Unknown C from how it grows, what it does to the medium and what it looks like under the microscope.

criteria.examined: Look at it under the microscope

assistant.title: Lab Assistant
assistant.setupDone: Medium, culture, tool and incubator are set for this challenge.

steps.takePlate: Take a plate from the rack.
steps.toBench: Bring the plate back to the bench to work on it.
steps.lightBurner: Light the Bunsen burner: it sterilises the loop and keeps airborne microbes off the plate.
steps.flame: Flame the loop to sterilise it.
steps.dip: Dip the loop in the culture.
steps.streak: Drag the loop across the agar. Flame it between quadrants for isolated colonies.
steps.dipSwab: Dip the swab in the culture.
steps.swab: Swab the whole plate for an even lawn.
steps.spread: Choose a dilution, then pipette and spread.
steps.closeLid: Close the lid so nothing lands on the agar.
steps.incubate: Move the plate to the incubator.
steps.play: Press Play and raise the speed to let time pass.
steps.wait: Growing… colonies appear after 10 to 16 hours.
steps.observe: Look closely: use Inspect, Ruler or Count.

warnings.lidOpenNoFlame: A lid is off and the burner is not lit: airborne microbes are settling on the agar.
warnings.flameFirst: This loop has not been flamed. It may carry microbes from the bench.
warnings.usedUnflamed: This plate was touched by an unflamed loop and may be contaminated.
warnings.wontGrow: This organism will not grow on the medium of this plate.
warnings.wrongMedium: This challenge works on a different medium. Take a new plate.

observations.noGrowth: Nothing has grown. Check the temperature and what was on the loop.
observations.noGrowthCold: Nothing has grown: it has been too cold. Most bacteria stop growing in the fridge.
observations.noGrowthSelective: Nothing has grown: this selective medium inhibits what you plated.
observations.lactosePositive: Pink to red colonies fermented lactose: the acid turns the indicator in the medium.
observations.lactoseNegative: Colourless colonies did not ferment lactose.
observations.mannitolPositive: The medium turned yellow where mannitol was fermented to acid.
observations.mannitolNegative: Growth without a colour change: mannitol was not fermented.

hemolysis.alpha: A greenish zone is alpha-hemolysis: the red cells are only partly broken down.
hemolysis.beta: A clear zone is beta-hemolysis: the red cells around the colony are completely lysed.
hemolysis.gamma: No change around the colonies is gamma-hemolysis: the red cells are untouched.

observations.pigmentCool: The red pigment is made because the plate grew at a cool temperature.
observations.pigmentWarm: These colonies are pale: this organism does not make its red pigment at body temperature.
observations.pigmentDiffuses: The green-blue tint in the agar is a pigment that dissolves in water and spreads out from the colonies.
observations.swarming: The spreading rings are swarming: highly motile cells move out over the agar in waves.
observations.swarmingSuppressed: On this medium the organism cannot swarm, so it forms ordinary colonies.
observations.mold: The fuzzy colony is a mold. Its centre darkens as spores form while the margin keeps growing.
observations.mucoid: Large, slimy colonies come from a thick capsule around the cells.
observations.contaminant: Something is growing that you did not put there: a contaminant.
observations.zones: Clear zones around discs show where the antibiotic stopped growth. Measure them with the Ruler.
observations.isolated: Separate colonies each grew from a single cell: these can be picked as pure cultures.
observations.confluent: Growth has merged into a lawn; single colonies cannot be told apart.

pure-culture.streaked: Dip the loop in Unknown A and streak a plate.
pure-culture.isolated: The colonies have not separated. Streak again in four quadrants, flaming the loop before each one and dragging out of the previous quadrant.

fleming.mold: Put a spot of Penicillium on the plate and incubate at 25 °C for about three days; molds are slow and dislike 37 °C.
fleming.staph: Now swab or streak Staphylococcus aureus across the same plate and incubate another day.
fleming.inhibited: The mold must be established before the bacteria are added. Let it grow longer, then add S. aureus.

kirby-bauer.lawn: Take a Mueller-Hinton plate, dip the swab in Unknown B and swab the whole plate.
kirby-bauer.discs: With the lid still off, choose the Disc tool and place at least three different antibiotics 24 mm apart.
kirby-bauer.incubated: Close the lid and incubate at 35 °C for 16 to 18 hours.
kirby-bauer.measured: Choose the Ruler and click each disc to measure its zone.

temperature.inoculated: Streak Serratia marcescens onto two plates.
temperature.cool: Leave one on the bench (or set the incubator to 25 °C) for a day or two.
temperature.warm: Put the other in the incubator at 37 °C for a day.

differential-media.plate: Take a MacConkey plate and streak an organism onto it.
differential-media.fermenter: Add a lactose fermenter such as Escherichia coli or Klebsiella pneumoniae.
differential-media.nonFermenter: Add a non-fermenter such as Salmonella enterica or Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

blood-agar.beta: Grow Streptococcus pyogenes or Staphylococcus aureus on blood agar.
blood-agar.alpha: Grow Streptococcus pneumoniae on blood agar. It likes CO₂.
blood-agar.gamma: Grow Staphylococcus epidermidis on blood agar.

count-cfu.spread: Choose the Spread tool, pick a dilution and spread 0.1 mL on a plate.
count-cfu.countable: Too many or too few colonies. The culture holds about 10⁹ cells per mL: which dilution puts 30 to 300 cells in 0.1 mL?
count-cfu.counted: Choose the Count tool and count the colonies.
count-cfu.plausible: Check the count: CFU/mL = colonies ÷ (0.1 mL × dilution).

aseptic.inoculated: Inoculate a plate with a pure culture.
aseptic.flamed: Flame the loop every time before it touches a culture or a plate. Start again with a new plate.
aseptic.incubated: Close the lid and incubate for 24 hours.
aseptic.clean: Something else got onto the plate. Work beside the lit burner, keep the lid off for as short a time as possible, and try a new plate.

mystery.cultured: Streak Unknown C. It is fastidious: which medium supports organisms that need enrichment?
mystery.examined: Use Inspect on a colony and prepare a Gram-stained slide.
mystery.identified: Compare the hemolysis, the Gram reaction and the cell arrangement with the fact cards, then choose the organism.

photoreal.name: Photoreal lab
photoreal.about: Glass, wet agar and bench lighting, as on a real bench.

stylized.name: Stylized
stylized.about: Soft colours, flat tones and outlines. Easiest to read.

bioluminescent.name: Bioluminescent
bioluminescent.about: A dark lab where each organism glows in its own colour.
